text:
Maria: quick heads up — I spotted inconsistent error "landing" between API responses and the console when requests get routed to a lower-tier model due to capacity/quota. thinking we should write a tiny playbook for how errors and signals land across API/SDK/console/dashboard.
Sam: can you paste a concrete divergence you saw?
Maria: sure — client got 200 with body {"routed":true, "note":"lower-tier"} while console showed a big "Degraded routing" banner. support folks were confused because API looked successful.
Jia: we should standardize an "error landing envelope": three parts — http status (where applicable), machine subcode (stable enum), and user_hint. e.g.
```
{
  "status": "ok",          // success vs error
  "subcode": "routed_degraded", // stable enum
  "routing_reason": "capacity", // capacity | quota | region | model_unavailable
  "user_hint": "We served a lower-latency model to keep latency SLOs — consider upgrading plan or retrying later"
}
```
Liz (devex): +1. Also recommend a consistent header so SDKs can quickly detect landing: `X-Redwood-Landing: routed_degraded` and `X-Redwood-Reason: quota`
Paul: telemetry-wise we must emit `landing_state` on traces/spans and as metric labels in the request pipeline. otherwise dashboards can't correlate support tickets -> signals.
Maria: important callout: quota-driven vs capacity-driven routing should be distinguishable. propose subcodes like `quota_soft_routing` vs `capacity_fallback`.
Sam: this brings up HTTP semantics — do we return 200 for degraded but successful generation, or return 409/429 for quota cases? my vote: keep 200 for successful text response, but include a stable header and subcode for programmatic handling. returning 4xx breaks a lot of clients.
Jia: agree on 200 for successful payloads. but SDKs should expose a first-class exception/path for subcodes tagged as `client_action_needed` (e.g., quota hard-limit). so spec must list which subcodes map to SDK exceptions.
Liz (devex): UX: console banners should reuse the same canonical copy for each subcode and link to an expanded panel explaining cause + remediation. also show an action button (open billing / change routing policy / retry).
Maria: rollout UX: when we change routing policies (canary), console should show a small timeline of recent routing events and % of requests landing in each state. that helps SRE/PMs understand impact.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Release routing-state-headers v1 -> staging at 2026-03-21T15:24:00Z (sha: a1b2c3)
Paul: QA ask — add unit/integration checks that assert header + body subcode + telemetry emitted when a route downgrade happens. I'll add to the release checklist.
Sam: backcompat note — older SDKs shouldn't break. so headers are additive and SDKs should ignore unknown subcodes. server should always provide metrics even if header omitted.
Liz (devex): :thumbsup: i'll mock up the console banner + panel and a tiny playbook for support (how to read subcode, dashboard widget to link) and post in #eng-design tomorrow.
Maria: thanks all. i'll open an RFC with: header names, subcode enum, mapping table -> SDK behaviors, dashboard panels and runbook snippets. please flag urgent objections in the thread.
